# EnterpriseGlue v0.15.2 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.15.1`.

## Highlights

- **plugin-installation-toolchain:** Rebuilds the Plugin Manager toolchain with patched Go components and permits protected package publication to reuse only content-identical immutable dependencies.

## User and administrator impact

- Plugin installer and manager images contain a patched ORAS build and the current Cosign patch release.
- A manager-only or installer-only package update no longer requires artificial version bumps for unchanged SDK and runtime packages.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Use plugin installer 0.2.1, Plugin Manager 0.1.1, and the matching 0.2.1 and 0.1.1 Helm charts; do not consume artifacts from the aborted 0.2.0/0.1.0 toolchain publication run.

## Database migrations

- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- ORAS 1.3.3 is compiled with the digest-pinned Go 1.26.6 toolchain instead of redistributing its vulnerable upstream binary.
- Cosign 3.1.3 is compiled with patched Go 1.26.6 plus fixed gRPC, x/mod, and x/text dependency floors instead of redistributing the vulnerable upstream binary.
- Existing npm package versions may be reused only when a freshly downloaded registry archive has the same canonical file tree, content, symlink targets, and executable bits as the local package; version collisions with different payloads fail closed.
- Pull requests that change the public installer or manager now build both images and fail on HIGH or CRITICAL vulnerabilities before protected publication.

## Documentation

- Container third-party notices record the patched ORAS build and Cosign version for both public toolchain images.

## Published packages

| Package | Previous | New | Impact |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `@enterpriseglue/plugin-installer` | `0.2.0` | `0.2.1` | patch |
| `@enterpriseglue/plugin-manager` | `0.1.0` | `0.1.1` | patch |

## Known limitations

- The aborted toolchain publication subjects remain unqualified and are not referenced by a release receipt or supported catalog entry.

## Rollback

- Restore the previous image and chart references only in an isolated test environment; the previous publication failed the protected vulnerability gate and is not supported.

## Validation evidence

- Plugin package publication planner unit tests and protected registry-integrity checks
- Multi-architecture installer and manager builds with architecture-neutral JavaScript dependency enforcement
- Protected Cosign verification, Trivy HIGH/CRITICAL gate, Helm payload verification, provenance attestations, and offline Zot import acceptance
